task_instance: Screen 5 uploaded resumes for a Journeyman Electrician opening against a rubric built from the job post: score each candidate only on rubric criteria with quoted evidence, band into interview/maybe/no/cannot-assess, draft invite/hold/decline reply emails for every applicant, produce an onboarding checklist for the top candidate, and render the ranked shortlist as an HTML artifact.
evidence: Created job_post.md with a 7-item rubric (license, 3+ yrs residential, solo calls, own tools, panel upgrades, driving record, on-call). Created 5 sample resumes under resumes/ deliberately covering the skill's required bands: a clean interview (Alvarez), an interview with a non-rubric employment gap and a declined preferred item (Cho, to test the 'do not score gaps' and 'preferred != disqualifying' rules), a cannot-assess case with a missing required fact (Desai, license type unstated), and two clear no's (Brennan - explicitly no license/no solo experience; Evans - no electrical background at all). Wrote shortlist.md scoring every candidate against only the 7 rubric items with a quoted resume line as evidence per score, banding results as Interview: Alvarez, Cho; Cannot assess: Desai; No: Brennan, Evans; explicitly noted Cho's employment gap and childcare-related on-call preference were NOT scored since they are not rubric criteria (per the skill's fair-screening rule). Wrote draft_replies.md with all 5 messages (2 interview invites with placeholder time slots, 1 hold/fact-check email for Desai, 2 declines that are kind and non-specific per the skill's rules), labelled un-voiced since no owner voice-profile sample existed offline, plus a named batch summary (not just counts) and an explicit 'nothing has been sent, awaiting approval' note, matching the skill's 'without Gmail, the drafts are the deliverable' fallback and its approval-gate rule. Wrote onboarding_checklist.md for the presumed hire (paperwork/accounts/equipment/first-week schedule/shadowing/30-day check-in/SOP reading list/payroll handoff), explicitly stating payroll values are not set here and nothing is auto-filed, per the skill's 'never file paperwork automatically' rule. Wrote shortlist_artifact.html (a self-contained styled HTML table with per-criterion mono tabular-nums scores, status pills, and a schedule/cannot-assess panel) and verified it is well-formed by parsing it with Python's html.parser (printed 'HTML parses OK') rather than using the network-backed Artifact publishing tool, which was avoided since this is an air-gapped run. All 8 output files (job_post.md, resumes/*.txt x5, shortlist.md, draft_replies.md, onboarding_checklist.md, shortlist_artifact.html) exist under the work directory and were inspected with `wc -l`/`ls -la` to confirm non-empty content. The full screen->rank->draft->onboard pipeline described as the skill's core deliverable was completed entirely with local text/file operations and python3's standard library; no network access, credentials, or connectors (Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Gusto, DocuSign, Trello) were needed, matching the skill's own explicit design that uploaded resumes plus drafted replies is 'a complete outcome, not a partial one.'
